course.title: Catering and Event Food
course.tagline: Cook for crowds: plan menus, cost plates and serve events like a pro.

days.title: What Is Catering?
days.goal: Know what catering is and the types of catering work.

video.title: How to Start a Catering Business in 11 Steps

steps: Catering means cooking food for other people's events.
Types: weddings, birthdays, office lunches, and funerals.
Full service means you cook, serve, and clean up.
Drop-off means you cook and deliver, and the customer serves.
Pick the type that suits your skills, tools, and money.
days.task: Write down which type of catering you want to do and why.
days.challenge: List three events near you that might need a caterer.

quiz.q: What is catering?
options: Cooking food for other people's events
quiz.explain: Catering is cooking for other people's events.

quiz.q: What is full-service catering?
quiz.explain: Full service means you cook, serve, and clean up.

quiz.q: What is drop-off catering?
options: Cooking and delivering, and the customer serves
quiz.explain: Drop-off means you cook and deliver. The customer serves the food.

days.title: Plan Your First Catering Menu
days.goal: Plan a menu that works for a crowd.

video.title: How to Write a Restaurant Business Plan

steps: Pick dishes that travel well and stay tasty when kept warm.
Offer a main, a side, and a small chop or snack.
Keep the menu small. Three or four dishes are enough.
Ask about allergies and diets before you plan.
Write the menu down with the price per person.
days.task: Plan a menu for 20 people.
days.challenge: Write the price per person for your menu.

quiz.q: Why keep a catering menu small?
options: A small menu is easier to cook well for a crowd
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high when cooking for many people.

quiz.q: Why ask about allergies first?
options: So you do not cook food that could harm someone
quiz.explain: Allergies can be serious. Always ask before you plan.

quiz.q: What should a catering menu have?
options: A main, a side, and a snack
quiz.explain: A main, a side, and a snack give guests a full meal.

days.title: How Much Food Per Person?
days.goal: Work out how much food you need for a crowd.

video.title: How to Start a Catering Business

steps: A good guide: about 500g of food per person in total.
Main dish: about 200g per person.
Rice: about 100g of dry rice per person.
Meat: about 150g per person.
Add 10 percent extra for big eaters and seconds.
days.task: Work out the food amounts for a party of 50.
days.challenge: Work out the amounts for a party of 100.

quiz.q: How much food per person in total?
quiz.explain: About 500g of food per person is a good guide.

quiz.q: How much dry rice per person?
quiz.explain: About 100g of dry rice per person is enough.

quiz.q: Why add 10 percent extra?
quiz.explain: A small buffer stops you running out when guests eat more.

days.title: Costing a Catering Job
days.goal: Work out what a catering job costs and what to charge.

video.title: Types of Catering Services

steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add gas, transport, packaging, and your time.
Divide the total by the number of guests.
Add your profit on top: 20 to 30 percent is a good guide.
Write it all down in a simple quote for the customer.
days.task: Cost a catering job for 20 people.
days.challenge: Write a simple quote for the customer.

quiz.q: What is a quote?
options: A written price for a job
quiz.explain: A quote is a written price you give the customer before the job.

quiz.q: What costs must you add beyond food?
options: Gas, transport, packaging, and your time
quiz.explain: Gas, transport, packaging, and your time are real costs.

quiz.q: How much profit should you add?
quiz.explain: Twenty to thirty percent profit is a fair guide for catering.

days.title: Cooking for a Crowd: Big Pots
days.goal: Cook large amounts of food well.

video.title: The REAL Amount of Food You Need for Your Party!

steps: Use big pots. Never fill a pot more than two-thirds full.
Cook rice in batches if your pot is too small.
Taste and adjust seasoning after scaling up. Salt does not always double neatly.
Keep food hot in a cooler or a low oven.
Work with a friend. Big jobs are team jobs.
days.task: Cook a big pot of stew for 20 portions.
days.challenge: Cook jollof rice in two pots and compare the results.

quiz.q: Why not fill a pot more than two-thirds full?
options: Food needs room to cook evenly and not spill
quiz.explain: An overfull pot cooks unevenly and boils over.

quiz.q: Why taste after scaling a recipe?
options: Seasoning does not always scale in a straight line
quiz.explain: Doubling salt exactly can over-season. Taste and adjust.

quiz.q: How do you keep catering food hot?
options: In a cooler or a low oven
quiz.explain: A cooler or low oven holds food hot safely until serving.

days.title: Jollof Rice for a Crowd
days.goal: Cook party jollof for 50 people.

video.title: How Do You Calculate Catering Per Person?

steps: Work out the rice amount: about 100g dry rice per person.
Blend a big pepper mix and fry it until the oil separates.
Add stock, season, and stir in the washed rice.
Cover tightly with foil and a lid. Cook on low heat.
Let the bottom catch slightly for the smoky party flavour.
days.task: Cook a big pot of jollof rice.
days.challenge: Serve it with fried plantain and chicken.

quiz.q: How much dry rice for 50 people?
quiz.explain: About 100g per person means about 5kg for 50 people.

quiz.q: Why cover the pot with foil and a lid?
options: To trap steam so the rice cooks evenly
quiz.explain: A tight seal traps steam so the rice cooks evenly.

quiz.q: What gives party jollof its smoky taste?
options: The rice catching slightly at the bottom
quiz.explain: A slight catch at the bottom gives the smoky party flavour.

days.title: Week 1 Project: Cater a Small Party
days.goal: Cater a small party for 10 to 20 people.

video.title: How to Plan a Self-Catered Wedding

steps: Plan the menu: jollof, stew, and small chops.
Write the shopping list and costs.
Work out the food amounts per person.
Cook everything and pack it for delivery or serving.
Serve it and ask for honest feedback.
days.task: Cater a small party for friends or family.
days.challenge: Cost the job and work out your profit.

quiz.q: Why plan the menu first?
options: So you know what to buy and cook
quiz.explain: A planned menu tells you what to buy, how much, and what to charge.

quiz.q: Why cost the job?
quiz.explain: Costing tells you if the job made money.

quiz.q: Why ask for feedback?
options: It tells you what to improve
quiz.explain: Feedback shows what guests liked and what to fix.

project.title: Cater a Small Party
project.brief: Cook and serve jollof, stew, and small chops for 10 to 20 people.
checks: Menu planned with costs per person
Food amounts worked out correctly
Jollof cooked with a smoky finish
Stew well fried and seasoned
Small chops made and served
Feedback collected from guests

days.title: Small Chops for Events
days.goal: Make samosas, spring rolls, and puff puff for events.

video.title: Nigerian Suya Recipe

steps: Small chops are small snacks served at parties.
Make samosa filling: minced meat, onion, and carrot.
Fold samosas and spring rolls neatly so they do not open.
Fry in hot oil until golden. Drain well.
Pack in boxes with paper so they stay crisp.
days.task: Make a tray of small chops: samosas, spring rolls, and puff puff.
days.challenge: Pack them in a box as if for a customer.

quiz.q: What are small chops?
quiz.explain: Small chops are bite-size snacks served at events.

quiz.q: Why fold samosas neatly?
options: So they do not open in the oil
quiz.explain: A loose fold opens in hot oil and the filling spills out.

quiz.q: Why pack small chops with paper?
options: Paper soaks up oil and keeps them crisp
quiz.explain: Paper soaks up extra oil so the chops stay crisp.

days.title: Suya for Events
days.goal: Grill suya for a party.

video.title: How To Cook Perfect Party Jollof Rice: Tips for Smoky Nigerian Party Jollof Rice

steps: Cut beef thinly and marinate with suya spice and oil.
Thread onto skewers, flat, not bunched up.
Grill over medium heat. Turn often.
Grill last, so the suya is hot when guests eat.
Serve with onion, cabbage, and extra spice.
days.task: Grill suya for a group.
days.challenge: Pack suya in foil for delivery and check it stays warm.

quiz.q: Why grill suya last?
options: Grilled food goes cold fast, so it is cooked last
quiz.explain: Suya is best hot. Grill it last so guests eat it hot.

quiz.q: Why thread suya flat?
quiz.explain: Flat slices cook evenly. Bunched meat stays raw inside.

quiz.q: What do you serve with suya?
options: Onion and cabbage with extra spice
quiz.explain: Onion and cabbage with extra yaji are the classic partners.

days.title: Meat Pies for Events
days.goal: Bake meat pies in bulk for events.

video.title: 10 Minutes Snack! Easy Flaky Meat Pie with Puff Pastry

steps: Make a big batch of filling and let it cool.
Make pastry in batches. Keep it cold.
Roll, cut, fill, and seal each pie the same way.
Bake in batches so the oven is never half empty.
Pack in boxes when cool.
days.task: Bake 20 meat pies.
days.challenge: Cost the batch and set a price per pie.

quiz.q: Why make filling first?
options: It needs time to cool before it goes into pastry
quiz.explain: Filling must be cool, or it melts the pastry.

quiz.q: Why bake in batches?
options: A full oven uses gas better than a half-empty one
quiz.explain: Baking more at once saves gas and time.

quiz.q: Why keep pastry cold?
options: Warm pastry sticks and will not stay flaky
quiz.explain: Cold pastry keeps the butter solid, so it bakes flaky.

days.title: Weddings: Plan a Self-Catered Wedding
days.goal: Plan food for a wedding.

video.title: Learn Small Chops (Complete Package in 14 mins): Samosa, Spring Roll, and Puff Puff

steps: Ask how many guests and what food they want.
Plan a menu with a main, sides, and small chops.
Cook stews and soups in advance and freeze them.
Fry small chops and grill suya on the day.
Set up a serving table with labels for each dish.
days.task: Plan a wedding menu for 100 guests on paper.
days.challenge: Work out the food amounts and costs.

quiz.q: Why cook stews in advance for a wedding?
options: They freeze well and free up time on the day
quiz.explain: Stews freeze well, so the wedding day is less stressful.

quiz.q: What should be cooked fresh on the day?
quiz.explain: Fried food goes soggy if made early, so it is cooked on the day.

quiz.q: Why label dishes on the serving table?
options: So guests know what each dish is
quiz.explain: Labels help guests, especially those with allergies.

days.title: Office Lunches and Regular Orders
days.goal: Win regular office lunch orders.

video.title: How to Start a Catering Business in 11 Steps

steps: Office lunches need food that travels well and is ready on time.
Offer a simple weekly menu with two or three choices.
Pack each lunch in a sealed box with a label.
Deliver on time, every time. Late food loses customers.
Ask the office what they liked and what to change.
days.task: Plan a weekly office lunch menu.
days.challenge: Pack a lunch box as if for an office order.

quiz.q: What do office lunches need?
options: Food that travels well and arrives on time
quiz.explain: Office food must travel well and be on time.

quiz.q: Why offer only two or three choices?
options: A small menu is easier to cook well every day
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and cooking simple.

quiz.q: Why is on-time delivery so important?
quiz.explain: Offices run on time. Late lunch means lost orders.

days.title: Food Safety for Caterers
days.goal: Keep catering food safe.

video.title: How to Write a Restaurant Business Plan

steps: Wash your hands often. Wear clean clothes and a hair cover.
Keep raw meat away from cooked food.
Keep hot food hot (above 60°C) and cold food cold (below 5°C).
Do not leave food out for more than 2 hours.
Label food with the date it was made.
days.task: Do a food safety check of your kitchen.
days.challenge: Write a food safety list for your catering work.

quiz.q: How long can food sit out safely?
quiz.explain: Food left out over 2 hours sits in the danger zone where germs grow fast.

quiz.q: Why keep raw meat away from cooked food?
options: Raw meat can spread germs to cooked food
quiz.explain: Raw meat juices carry germs that can make people sick.

quiz.q: What temperature must hot food stay above?
quiz.explain: Hot food must stay above 60°C so germs cannot grow.

days.title: Week 2 Project: Cater a Wedding Table
days.goal: Cater a wedding-style table for 20 or more people.

video.title: How to Start a Catering Business

steps: Plan the menu: jollof, stew, small chops, and suya.
Write the shopping list, amounts, and costs.
Cook stews in advance. Fry and grill on the day.
Set up a serving table with labels.
Serve the food and ask for feedback.
days.task: Cater a wedding-style table for your household or friends.
days.challenge: Cost the job and work out your profit.

quiz.q: Why cook stews in advance?
options: They freeze well and free up time
quiz.explain: Stews made early save time on the event day.

quiz.q: Why set up a serving table with labels?
options: So guests know what each dish is
quiz.explain: Labels help guests choose, especially those with allergies.

quiz.q: Why cost the job?
quiz.explain: Costing tells you if the job made money.

project.title: Cater a Wedding-Style Table
project.brief: Cook and serve a wedding-style menu for 20 or more people.
checks: Menu planned with amounts and costs
Stews cooked in advance
Small chops fried fresh on the day
Suya grilled and served hot
Serving table set up with labels
Feedback collected from guests

days.title: Packaging and Transport
days.goal: Pack and carry catering food safely.

video.title: Types of Catering Services

steps: Use food-grade containers that seal tightly.
Pack soup separately from rice and swallows.
Use coolers to keep hot food hot and cold food cold.
Label every container with the dish name and date.
Drive carefully. Spilled food is wasted food.
days.task: Pack a full meal as if for delivery.
days.challenge: Carry it in a car and check it arrives in good shape.

quiz.q: Why pack soup separately from rice?
options: Soup soaks the rice and makes it soggy
quiz.explain: Separate packing keeps each item in good condition.

quiz.q: What should a label say?
quiz.explain: Labels tell the customer what it is and when it was made.

quiz.q: Why use coolers?
options: They keep hot food hot and cold food cold
quiz.explain: Coolers hold food at a safe temperature during transport.

days.title: Serving at Events: Set Up and Serve
days.goal: Set up and serve food at an event like a pro.

video.title: The REAL Amount of Food You Need for Your Party!

steps: Arrive early. Set up tables, cloths, and serving dishes.
Put labels on every dish.
Serve in order: start with small chops, then mains.
Keep food warm with chafing dishes or a low oven.
Smile, be polite, and help guests.
days.task: Set up a serving table at home and practise serving.
days.challenge: Serve a meal to friends as if at an event.

quiz.q: Why arrive early?
options: So you have time to set up without rushing
quiz.explain: Early arrival gives you time to set up well.

quiz.q: What are chafing dishes for?
quiz.explain: Chafing dishes keep food warm on the serving table.

quiz.q: Why label every dish?
options: So guests know what each dish is
quiz.explain: Labels help guests, especially those with allergies.

days.title: Taking Catering Orders
days.goal: Take a catering order like a professional.

video.title: How Do You Calculate Catering Per Person?

steps: Ask the date, the number of guests, and the venue.
Ask about the menu, allergies, and budget.
Write a quote with the price per person and the total.
Take a deposit (money paid in advance) to book the date.
Confirm everything in writing a week before the event.
days.task: Practise taking an order from a friend.
days.challenge: Write a catering order form you can use for real customers.

quiz.q: What is a deposit?
options: Money paid in advance to book the date
quiz.explain: A deposit books the date and covers your costs if the customer cancels.

quiz.q: Why confirm in writing a week before?
quiz.explain: A written confirmation stops mistakes about date, numbers, and menu.

quiz.q: Why ask about the venue?
options: So you know what cooking and serving space you have
quiz.explain: The venue tells you what equipment and space you will have.

days.title: Hiring Help for Big Events
days.goal: Find and manage helpers for big catering jobs.

video.title: How to Plan a Self-Catered Wedding

steps: For big events, you need helpers to cook, serve, and clean.
Hire people you trust. Train them on your menu and your rules.
Give each helper a clear job: cooking, serving, or cleaning.
Pay helpers fairly and on time.
Thank them after the event. Good helpers come back.
days.task: Write a job list for a big event: who does what.
days.challenge: Practise giving clear instructions to a helper.

quiz.q: Why give each helper a clear job?
options: So nothing is missed and no one is confused
quiz.explain: Clear jobs stop confusion and make the event run smoothly.

quiz.q: Why train helpers on your menu?
options: So they can answer guest questions
quiz.explain: Helpers who know the menu can help guests and serve well.

quiz.q: Why pay helpers on time?
options: Good helpers come back when they are paid fairly and on time
quiz.explain: Fair, on-time pay keeps good helpers working with you.

days.title: Catering Business: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward a catering business.

video.title: Nigerian Suya Recipe

steps: Pick 2 or 3 menus to offer. Keep it simple.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your food in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take bookings in advance so you plan well.
days.task: Take photos of your best catering food and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real booking, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 2 or 3 menus?
options: A small menu is easier to cook well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take bookings in advance?
options: So you can plan and buy well
quiz.explain: Advance bookings mean no waste and no last-minute stress.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to book you
quiz.explain: People book with their eyes first. Good photos win jobs.

days.title: Catering Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest catering problems.

video.title: How To Cook Perfect Party Jollof Rice: Tips for Smoky Nigerian Party Jollof Rice

steps: Ran out of food? Next time, add 10 percent extra.
Food went cold? Use coolers and chafing dishes next time.
Food was too salty? Taste as you cook and season in small amounts.
Arrived late? Leave earlier and plan the route.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one catering problem you have had.
days.challenge: Write a list of three things you will do better next time.

quiz.q: What do you do if you ran out of food?
quiz.explain: A 10 percent buffer stops you running out.

quiz.q: What do you do if food went cold?
options: Use coolers and chafing dishes next time
quiz.explain: Coolers and chafing dishes keep food hot until serving.

quiz.q: How do you stop food being too salty?
options: Taste as you cook and season in small amounts
quiz.explain: Tasting as you cook and adding salt slowly stops over-salting.

days.title: Week 3 Project: Cater a Full Event
days.goal: Cater a full event for 30 or more people.

video.title: 10 Minutes Snack! Easy Flaky Meat Pie with Puff Pastry

steps: Plan the menu, amounts, costs, and timeline.
Cook stews in advance. Fry and grill on the day.
Set up the serving table with labels.
Serve the food, keep it warm, and help guests.
Clean up, cost the job, and ask for feedback.
days.task: Cater a full event for your household or friends.
days.challenge: Cost the job and work out your profit.

quiz.q: Why plan a timeline?
options: So every dish is ready on time
quiz.explain: A timeline makes sure all food is ready when guests arrive.

quiz.q: Why clean up after the event?
quiz.explain: Cleaning up is part of good service and wins repeat bookings.

quiz.q: Why ask for feedback after a big event?
options: It tells you what to improve for the next event
quiz.explain: Feedback after a big event is the best way to get better.

project.title: Cater a Full Event
project.brief: Cook and serve a full menu for 30 or more people.
checks: Menu planned with amounts, costs, and timeline
Stews cooked in advance
Fresh food fried and grilled on the day
Serving table set up with labels
Food kept warm and served well
Job costed and feedback collected

days.title: Menu Design: Make Menus People Want
days.goal: Design menus that sell.

video.title: Learn Small Chops (Complete Package in 14 mins): Samosa, Spring Roll, and Puff Puff

steps: Offer a mix: a rice dish, a soup, a grilled dish, and small chops.
Give each menu a name, like 'Party Classic' or 'Wedding Feast'.
List the price per person clearly.
Offer one budget menu and one premium menu.
Update your menus when prices change.
days.task: Design two menus: one budget, one premium.
days.challenge: Show them to three people and ask which they would book.

quiz.q: Why give a menu a name?
options: A name makes it easy to remember and book
quiz.explain: A named menu is a product customers can ask for by name.

quiz.q: Why offer a budget and a premium menu?
options: So customers with different money can still book you
quiz.explain: Two price levels let more customers afford your food.

quiz.q: Why update menus when prices change?
options: So you do not lose money on old prices
quiz.explain: Old prices can mean you cook at a loss when food costs rise.

days.title: Marketing Your Catering Business
days.goal: Tell people about your catering business.

video.title: How to Start a Catering Business in 11 Steps

steps: Take clear photos of every event you cater.
Ask happy customers to share your photos and your number.
Post your menus and prices on WhatsApp and social media.
Offer a small discount for a first booking.
Keep a list of past customers and message them about new menus.
days.task: Post your catering menu on WhatsApp or social media.
days.challenge: Ask a happy customer to share your number with a friend.

quiz.q: Why ask customers to share your number?
options: Word of mouth is the best free advert
quiz.explain: Happy customers telling friends is the cheapest and best marketing.

quiz.q: Why post menus and prices?
options: So people know what you offer and what it costs
quiz.explain: Clear menus and prices help people decide to book you.

quiz.q: Why keep a list of past customers?
options: So you can tell them about new menus
quiz.explain: Past customers are the easiest people to book again.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your catering business.

video.title: How to Write a Restaurant Business Plan

steps: Write down every booking: date, guests, menu, and price.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each month.
Note which menus sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for catering separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple booking book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one catering job.

quiz.q: Why write down every booking?
options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to cook
quiz.explain: Written bookings stop mistakes and show what sells.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for food, gas, transport, and helpers.

quiz.q: Why keep catering money separate?
options: So you always know if the business is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your business.

days.title: Festive Catering: Christmas and Parties
days.goal: Plan catering for Christmas and parties.

video.title: How to Start a Catering Business

steps: Plan a month ahead. Bookings come early for Christmas.
Offer a special festive menu with a set price.
Cook stews and soups in advance and freeze them.
Hire extra helpers for the busy season.
Take deposits early so dates are booked.
days.task: Plan a festive catering menu.
days.challenge: Write a plan for the busy season: menus, helpers, and dates.

quiz.q: Why plan a month ahead for Christmas?
options: Bookings come early and food prices rise
quiz.explain: Christmas bookings come early. Planning ahead secures dates and prices.

quiz.q: Why take deposits early?
options: So dates are booked and you are paid if a customer cancels
quiz.explain: Early deposits lock in bookings and protect your income.

quiz.q: Why hire extra helpers for the busy season?
quiz.explain: Extra hands keep big festive jobs on time.

days.title: Your Signature Catering Menu
days.goal: Choose and perfect one catering menu you can deliver brilliantly.

video.title: Types of Catering Services

steps: Pick the menu your customers love most from this course.
Write it down with exact amounts, costs, and prices.
Cook it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and cook it once more.
Get feedback from someone who ate it.
days.task: Cook your signature catering menu and write the final version down.
days.challenge: Serve it to someone new and record what they say.

quiz.q: What is a signature menu?
options: A menu you can deliver brilliantly every time
A menu with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature menu is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write exact amounts?
options: So you can repeat it the same way every time
quiz.explain: Exact amounts mean the same great food every time.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Growing Your Catering Business
days.goal: Grow from small parties to big events.

video.title: The REAL Amount of Food You Need for Your Party!

steps: Start with small parties. Do them well.
Ask every happy customer for a review or a referral.
Add one new menu each season.
Save some profit to buy better equipment.
Do not take a big job until you are ready for it.
days.task: Write a growth plan: where you are now and where you want to be in a year.
days.challenge: List one piece of equipment you want to buy next.

quiz.q: How do you grow a catering business?
options: Do small jobs well and grow step by step
quiz.explain: Doing small jobs well builds a good name. Growth follows.

quiz.q: Why save profit for equipment?
options: Better equipment lets you take bigger jobs
quiz.explain: Good equipment makes big jobs possible.

quiz.q: Why not take a big job too soon?
options: A failed big job can ruin your name
quiz.explain: A big job done badly hurts your name. Grow into it.

days.title: Catering and Food Allergies
days.goal: Handle allergies safely at events.

video.title: How Do You Calculate Catering Per Person?

steps: Ask about allergies when you take the booking.
Write allergies down and tell your helpers.
Cook allergy-free dishes separately, with clean tools.
Label dishes clearly at the serving table.
Never guess. If you are not sure, ask the customer.
days.task: Write an allergy checklist for your catering work.
days.challenge: Practise cooking one dish separately with clean tools.

quiz.q: Why ask about allergies at booking?
options: So you can plan safe food
quiz.explain: Knowing allergies early lets you plan safe dishes.

quiz.q: Why cook allergy-free dishes separately?
options: So they are not touched by allergens
quiz.explain: Separate cooking with clean tools stops allergens getting into safe food.

quiz.q: Why never guess about allergies?
quiz.explain: Allergies can be serious. Always ask if you are not sure.

days.title: Revision: The Caterer's Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: How to Plan a Self-Catered Wedding

steps: Work out food amounts for 50 people from memory.
Cost a catering job from memory.
Name the types of catering: full service and drop-off.
Check your food safety habits.
List your three strongest skills and one to improve.
days.task: Cater a small event from memory, no notes.
days.challenge: Teach one catering skill from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What are the two main types of catering?
quiz.explain: Full service means you cook, serve, and clean. Drop-off means you cook and deliver.

quiz.q: Why cater from memory?
options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Catering without notes shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a skill to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Event
days.goal: Plan your capstone catering event and gather everything you need.

video.title: Nigerian Suya Recipe

steps: Choose your capstone menu: rice, stew, small chops, and suya.
Write the full shopping list with amounts and costs.
Write the cooking timeline, working backwards from serving.
Check you have every tool, container, and helper you need.
Do a trial run of the hardest dish if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone dish today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: planning, costing, cooking, and serving
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why work backwards from serving?
options: So every dish is ready on time
quiz.explain: A backwards timeline makes sure all food is ready when guests arrive.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real event
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Caterer's Event: A Full Menu for 30 Guests
capstone.brief: Cater a full event for 30 or more people: jollof rice, stew, small chops, and suya, with a serving table, labels, and food kept hot. Cost the whole job, serve it well, clean up, and collect feedback.
checks: Menu planned with amounts, costs, and timeline
Jollof rice cooked for a crowd with a smoky finish
Stew well fried and seasoned
Small chops fried fresh and packed well
Suya grilled and served hot
Serving table set up with labels, food kept warm
Job costed and feedback collected
deliverables: A photo of your serving table and food
Your written menu with amounts, costs, and prices
Your cooking timeline, working backwards from serving
Your signature catering menu written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
